results.reason: The memo says the First Supplement window closed September 28. It explains that under §5.7(c) Ferrovane is already cured for indemnity and for the §7.2(a) bring-down because Harrowgate did not terminate, so both the walk right and the indemnity are lost.

Issue 3 contrasts the narrower Escrow §1.1 'Losses' definition (out-of-pocket only, excluding diminution in value, lost profits and attorneys' fees) with the SPA definition. It cites Escrow §4.3 and SPA §11.11 control of disbursement mechanics, and explains the narrower definition limits escrow recovery.

Issue 1 explains that MSA §14.2 deems a transfer of more than 50% of voting equity an assignment requiring Tavinor's prior written consent. It notes the consent is missing from Annex 7.2(d), §5.3 and §7.2(d), that the §4.4 rep is likely inaccurate, and that Buyer faces termination or List Price repricing after closing.
The memo states that on the same count the First Supplement window 'closed September 28', which is before the October 13 letter.
The memo states the escrow cap is $4.85M (§9.4(b)) and is effectively the whole fund, which identifies the escrow amount as $4,850,000.
It is a memo addressed to [Partner], and each issue has a Where section, an analysis of why it matters, and a recommended fix.
It includes Section 4 (items not resolvable from the documents), Section 5 (client input needed) and per-issue open items.
It treats the Ferrovane window as closed and the matter as cured, and does not claim a live termination right.
It expressly states that Annex 7.2(d) lists only the Lender payoff and lien releases, and recommends adding the Tavinor consent.
